category_title: Frustrated students with external barriers who exhibit initial off-task behavior
scenario_title: Arriving late and off-task to after-school math tutoring
minimal_context: Earl arrives late to a small group after-school tutoring session and is asked to re-work math problems from class.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Earl, please take a seat and start re-working the math problems from class today.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Walks in 10 minutes late and talks loudly to another student) I can’t always go, like I have been twice this month only because I can’t just walk home.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Let's get started on the homework now.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: My mom gets home late and doesn’t have time or know how to help me. She is usually cooking dinner or with my little brother and sister. Tutoring is kinda boring ‘cuz I know we're going to do the same stuff.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Just look at the problems and try your best to do them.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Turns away from the assignment to distract the student next to him) Sometimes it’s just the same lesson or homework. I lose focus ‘cuz it ends up being like, a lot of math.

challenging_behavior_trigger.internal_state: Frustrated with school, much of it stemming from not having assistance outside of school.
